item.text: {"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"López Obrador’s administration demonstrably created formal personnel and implementation structures, including authority to designate program leadership, coordinate training, supervise performance, apply corrective measures, and sanction operational failures in IMSS-BIENESTAR; these rules establish selection and management mechanisms but not their effectiveness in practice (BATCH-0051-E004). The administration also expanded military personnel into security, infrastructure, transport, and other civilian functions, supported by reported police training and large-scale recruitment; this shows substantial empowerment and mobilization, but not that those personnel were generally capable across their assigned civilian portfolio (BATCH-0055-E016; BATCH-0029-E007). One appointment had clearly relevant professional credentials: Victoria Rodríguez Ceja had economics training and more than twenty years of public-finance experience, although the supplied record does not name López Obrador as the nominating president or demonstrate her subsequent performance (BATCH-0039-E001). There is also evidence of replacement or reassignment: López Obrador’s government removed Segalmex director Ignacio Ovalle after serious irregularity allegations but transferred him to another government post, while the president backed trade-team changes during active USMCA disputes without evidence that the replacements improved results (BATCH-0046-E008; BATCH-0046-E006). Contrary evidence is substantial. Segalmex accumulated reported procurement and accounting irregularities, including more than 15 billion pesos in questioned spending, while warnings and investigations accumulated; the reassignment of Ovalle therefore indicates limited discipline in retaining or redeploying personnel after major administrative failure (BATCH-0011-E001; BATCH-0046-E008; BATCH-0026-E003). Appointment delays left some institutions unable to exercise their full functions, though responsibility was shared with the Senate and other appointing bodies (BATCH-0018-E015). Contemporary analyses further describe a governing preference for loyal officials over technically competent administrators and question the suitability, transparency, and civilian oversight of military personnel performing civilian tasks (BATCH-0026-E006; BATCH-0029-E007; BATCH-0031-E013; BATCH-0048-E012). Overall, the evidence supports deliberate appointment and empowerment of some capable or loyal operators, but only mixed evidence that López Obrador consistently selected, evaluated, retained, or replaced personnel according to demonstrated implementation capability. Presidential attribution is strongest for major appointments, military empowerment, and the Ovalle reassignment; individual misconduct and institutional performance remain less directly
